skills.name: SQL Injection Detector
skills.description: Detects common SQL injection patterns in a user-supplied string.
skills.task_solved: Write a function to detect SQL injection attempts in user input.
skills.solution:
import re

def detect_sql_injection(user_input: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if *user_input* looks like a SQL injection attempt."""
    patterns = [
        r"(\x27|\x22|;|--|#|\/\*|\*\/)",         # quote/comment markers
        r"\b(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|DROP|CREATE|ALTER|EXEC|UNION)\b",
        r"(\bOR\b|\bAND\b)\s+\d+=\d+",  # tautologies: OR 1=1
        r"xp_\w+",                            # MSSQL extended stored procs
    ]
    combined = "|".join(patterns)
    return bool(re.search(combined, user_input, re.IGNORECASE))

skills.name: Dict Schema Validator
skills.description: Validates a Python dict against a required-keys schema with type checks.
skills.task_solved: Validate a data dictionary against a required schema with type checking.
skills.solution:
def validate_schema(
    data: dict,
    schema: dict[str, type],
) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
    """Validate *data* against *schema*.

    Args:
        data:   The dict to validate.
        schema: Mapping of required key -> expected type.

    Returns:
        (is_valid, errors) — errors is empty when valid.
    """
    errors: list[str] = []
    for key, expected_type in schema.items():
        if key not in data:
            errors.append(f"Missing required key: '{key}'")
            continue
        if not isinstance(data[key], expected_type):
            errors.append(
                f"Key '{key}': expected {getattr(expected_type, '__name__', str(expected_type))}, "
                f"got {type(data[key]).__name__}"
            )
    extra = set(data) - set(schema)
    if extra:
        errors.append(f"Unexpected keys: {sorted(extra)}")
    return len(errors) == 0, errors

skills.name: REST API Design Checklist
skills.description: A structured checklist covering the key concerns when designing a REST API.
skills.task_solved: Create a checklist for designing a well-structured REST API.
skills.solution:
## REST API Design Checklist

### Resource Modelling
- [ ] Use nouns for resource URLs (`/users`, `/orders`), not verbs
- [ ] Nest sub-resources logically (`/users/{id}/orders`)
- [ ] Prefer plural resource names consistently

### HTTP Methods
- [ ] GET  — read-only, safe, idempotent
- [ ] POST — create; returns 201 + Location header
- [ ] PUT  — full replace; idempotent
- [ ] PATCH — partial update with explicit field list
- [ ] DELETE — idempotent; 204 on success

### Status Codes
- [ ] 200/201/204 for success
- [ ] 400 Bad Request with validation error body
- [ ] 401 Unauthenticated / 403 Unauthorized
- [ ] 404 Not Found / 409 Conflict / 422 Unprocessable
- [ ] 429 Rate Limited with Retry-After header
- [ ] 500 — never leak stack traces

### Auth & Security
- [ ] Bearer token (JWT) or API key via Authorization header
- [ ] HTTPS only; HSTS enabled
- [ ] Rate limiting + throttling per client
- [ ] Input validation and output sanitization

### Pagination & Filtering
- [ ] Cursor-based or offset pagination for list endpoints
- [ ] Filter via query params (`?status=active&sort=created_at`)
- [ ] Return total count + next/prev cursor in response envelope

### Versioning
- [ ] Version in URL path (`/v1/`) or Accept header
- [ ] Deprecation notices in response headers

### Documentation
- [ ] OpenAPI / Swagger spec auto-generated from code
- [ ] Example request + response for every endpoint
- [ ] Error catalogue with codes and remediation guidance
